newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada raw materials prices rise 2.5 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Canada raw materials prices rise 2.5 pct in May.

text.p: issued the following economic indicators for February, base
INDEX Month pct Yr pct May index

The raw materials price index reflects the prices paid by manufacturers for key raw materials. Unlike the industrial product price index, the raw materials price index includes goods that are not produced in Canada.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast that the overall index would rise 1.8 percent in May from April.

Statistics Canada said that in May higher prices were noted for all major groupings, with crude oil providing the major contribution. Excluding mineral fuels, raw material prices would have risen 1.7 percent.

The federal agency said that in May, the major contributors to higher monthly prices were crude oil, copper, aluminum materials, logs, pulpwood and hogs. Lower prices for rubber, iron ore, radioactive lead concentrates partly offset the overall monthly increase.
